audioDescription: Silent preview: no audio track. Authored silent cue sequence: idle sway 0–0.6s, rarity tier steps at 0.8/1.0/1.2s, charge squash 1.2–1.8s, burst hit at 1.8s, links snap 2.15–2.5s, hold to 3s.
limitations: Scene-dependent background (BACKGROUND_REVIEW refresh): a cool mint studio cyclorama made of two flat screen-space bands, wall #C9E0DA and floor #AFCFC8, drawn in the contour pass wherever there is no geometry depth. It follows the reviewed lessons of a mid-light low-chroma ground, a warm saturated hero, a dark stable outline and a product-turntable cyclorama, without copying any source subject. #F4ECD9 is kept as a material colour (highlight band, bonds, card) rather than as the canvas.
Illustrative procedural scene: spheres, cylinders and discs are built in Three.js; no physical materials, lighting or modelled assets.

Toon bands are an explicit palette mapping: a 3-step DataTexture ramp in MeshToonMaterial selects foreground #26394A shadow, the base token, or a background #F4ECD9 highlight; the rim light is a discrete fresnel band, not physical lighting.

Contours come from a screen-space depth+normal edge ShaderPass (3 px at 720p), soft-edged over 8 taps; a separate normal/depth render target is used instead of WebGL MRT. Very thin bonds at grazing angles can show slightly heavier lines.

Glow card is flat stepped discs (accent_1 outer band, #F4ECD9 inner band), with no bloom or gradient. The rarity 'background tone' swap is applied to the halo/card backing behind the hero; the cyclorama wall/floor stays fixed so the background never moves.
Burst particles are 16 seeded (mulberry32) toon spheres launched from 1.3× the hero radius and shrinking away by about 2.5s; no physics simulation.

The cream-face outlined title of the reference illustration is rendered as a solid #26394A HTML heading on the #C9E0DA wall (8.6:1 contrast); wording is unchanged. The cream bonds and particles have low hue contrast against the wall (1.2:1) and are separated by the dark contour.
Three.js internals (UUID generation, Clock) contain Math.random/performance.now but do not affect rendered pixels; every frame is evaluated from GSAP timeline time on onUpdate and hf-seek.
The 3-second preview omits the collection step; the full video would extend each stage and add collection.
The recipe demonstrated is cartoon_reward; Blender was not used. Renderer: Three.js MeshToonMaterial plus an EffectComposer ShaderPass, chosen from the installed TECHNOLOGY_POOL entries.
